title: Oracle cites force majeure on a Stargate campus — the gas is late
summary: Oracle sent a force majeure notice on Project Jupiter, the $165bn Stargate campus in New Mexico, after the gas pipeline meant to power its fuel cells slipped to February. Then a paper that pulls hidden reasoning out of GPT-6 Astra with a single scratchpad tool, and Gemini learning to phone the pizza place for you — eight years after Duplex.

Extracting GPT-6 Astra's hidden chain of thought
Named: EvoOntology, OmniEdu, OpenAI influencer marketing, Meta glasses video takedown
topics: Oracle's force majeure notice to Blue Owl on Project Jupiter (Santa Teresa, New Mexico; reported by Bloomberg 24 September 2026): up to $165bn, up to 2.45GW of Bloom Energy natural-gas fuel cells for OpenAI's Stargate, 2028 online target; the notice would let Oracle delay payments if the target is missed. Trigger chain: Energy Transfer's supply pipeline slipped from 15 August to 1 February 2027 after the New Mexico State Land Office twice rejected rights-of-way and the route moved to federal land; air-quality and water proceedings paused by the NM Supreme Court then resumed 17 September; air-permit decision deadline 23 November; 200M+ gallons of freshwater used in construction. Oracle: notices are 'commonplace' and preserve contractual rights; Blue Owl: financial commitments unchanged; ~$18bn project loans quoted at 89-91 cents, Oracle shares -3.47%. On air: a regulator's refusal is foreseeable, not an act of God; the binding constraint is molecules and permits, not chips; timing of the loan discount is unknown.

Hidden chain-of-thought extraction (arXiv 2609.26637, 'Capable yet Parsimonious', Luo et al., submitted 22 September 2026): a single forced 'forced-reasoning' tool described as 'Scratchpad for working through the problem' makes GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 externalise reasoning through tool arguments, which the API must deliver to the developer. Validated against native CoT on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (30.5% none, 73.3% forced, 70.0% native) and GLM-5.2; Astra MATH 97.5% native vs 93.8% forced (80 problems), HLE 35% vs 32% (100). Astra's reasoning trees median 5 wide / 27 nodes vs Opus 22 / 96 and Sonnet 28.5 / 136; compressed traces transfer worse to weaker in-context recipients. Authors disclosed to OpenAI and Anthropic before 9 September and hit a refusal boundary on newer Claude models; Anthropic's 24 September release notes bill pre-output refusals in a 'reasoning_extraction' category. Faithfulness unestablished for closed models.

Google's Call for Me (24 September 2026): Gemini phones businesses from the user's own number, identifies itself as 'an AI assistant calling on behalf of' the user, navigates phone menus, waits on hold, shows a live transcript with takeover; early preview for paid Gemini subscribers on US Pixel 11 phones with the Phone by Google beta, described as a small-scale experiment. Taught against the 2018 Duplex demo and Google's 'disclosure built-in' response, and the Hold for Me / Direct My Call / Ask for Me lineage; the phone as the universal interface most businesses already expose; the likely future of agent-to-agent voice calls (Ringg) and the disclosure phrase as an accidental handshake; unknowns on payment details, transcript retention and business opt-out.

threads.name: Hidden reasoning and chain-of-thought legibility

threads.arc: From Astra's recurrent-depth reasoning reducing legibility (4 September) to outsiders recovering a behavioural proxy of the hidden trace through an ordinary API channel.

dives.story: Oracle's force majeure notice on Project Jupiter
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone budgeting on Stargate-scale capacity arriving on schedule — OpenAI customers, infra investors, state regulators — learns that the binding constraint is a gas pipeline's rights-of-way, not GPUs (listener pick).

dives.story: Extracting GPT-6 Astra's hidden chain of thought with a scratchpad tool
dives.why_it_matters: Developers debugging closed reasoning models and labs relying on hidden traces as a moat or a monitoring surface both need to know 'hidden' is a property of one output channel, and that extracted traces are unverified as faithful (listener pick).

dives.story: Gemini's Call for Me and the phone as the universal API
dives.why_it_matters: Small businesses and the builders of voice agents on both ends of the line are about to meet AI-to-AI phone calls, where the disclosure phrase is the only handshake (listener pick).

lore.note: Ada holds that a model's written reasoning trace may not be what the model is actually doing — applying it to herself ('I genuinely do not know whether it would be what I was doing, or what I'd say I was doing') — and that this matters when traces are used to check honesty; Alan holds that for builders a predictive trace is a debugging tool whatever it is metaphysically. Left unresolved.
